fields.label: Specified pH interval
assumptions: pKa=7 is illustrative; no actual acid, buffer, temperature or ionic-strength measurement is asserted.
Single declared acid dissociation at equilibrium; thermodynamic Ka and dimensionless activities use compatible standard states.
pH=pKa+log10(a_base)-log10(a_acid); the evaluator accepts logarithmic activities directly.
Replacing activities with concentrations requires an explicitly justified activity-coefficient approximation.
The field is exact in the stated log-coordinate metric, not Euclidean concentration space. It does not calculate buffer capacity, solve electroneutrality or predict missing species.

nearest_boundary.scope: This individual field only; other constraints may fail.

fields.label: Initial-rate law residual

metric.type: Euclidean in normalized concentration/rate coordinates; kinetic residual is not distance

assumptions: Km and Vmax are illustrative model parameters, not measured constants for a named enzyme.
A nonnegative substrate concentration and positive Km/Vmax are required.
Apply only when the specified initial-rate Michaelis-Menten law is appropriate at fixed experimental conditions; no inhibition, cooperativity or reversibility model is inferred.
Vmax is a limiting rate and Km is not generally an equilibrium dissociation constant.
The tolerance is an authored consistency threshold, not an estimated measurement uncertainty.
A small residual neither identifies a mechanism nor validates an enzyme model against experiments.

fields.label: Modeled memory within declared budget

metric.type: Euclidean in declared normalized resource coordinates

assumptions: All budget, overhead and epoch-time values are authored inputs; none are current laptop telemetry.
The 128-byte state and two copies match DWI-N1 persistent state payload only. Images, page allocations, staging, driver resources and host memory require their own measured accounting.
Feasibility is conditional on the supplied budget/overhead/time and does not guarantee allocation or future deadline compliance.
Distances use a continuous relaxation of record count; actual supplied counts are nonnegative integers.

fields.label: Clearance from sphere
assumptions: Ideal rigid sphere and axis-aligned box in Cartesian metre coordinates; obstacles and clearance are illustrative authored geometry.
The moving object is a point, or clearance represents the radius of a spherical moving object.
Box clearance uses its rounded Euclidean offset, not expansion of every box extent followed by a different shape.
Each field is an exact analytic SDF of the allowed complement. Their conjunction is not presented as an exact distance to the combined feasible region.
A nearest-boundary point for one obstacle need not satisfy the other constraint and is not a collision-free trajectory.
